questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, make sure that:

options.text: The emergency exits are hard to open.
The emergency exit warning devices work properly.
The emergency exits cannot be reached from inside the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency exit warning devices work properly.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, emergency exit warning devices must work correctly. All emergency exits should open smoothly, be in good condition, and close securely from inside the bus.

questions.question: When doing the stop and start maneuver during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Cut off other vehicles to get onto the shoulder if needed.
Slam on the brakes to stop as fast as possible.

questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, you will pull over to the side of the road and stop. To do this correctly, check traffic, turn on your signal, slow down gradually with even braking, change gears as needed, and come to a full stop without coasting.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following except:

options.text: Complete the test without a moving violation.
Obey all traffic signs and signals only when other traffic is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey all traffic signs and signals only when other traffic is present.
questions.explanation: You must drive safely during the on-road driving test. This means wearing your safety belt, obeying all traffic signs and signals at all times, following all traffic laws, and finishing the test without an accident or moving violation.

questions.question: Which of the following is not acceptable emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three liquid burning flares, and a fire extinguisher that is properly charged and rated.

questions.question: In a school bus, where is the overhead inside rearview mirror located?

options.text: Above the windshield on the driver's side of the bus
Above the door on the passenger side of the bus
Above the emergency door in the rear

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield on the driver's side of the bus
questions.explanation: On a school bus, the overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted directly above the windshield on the driver's side. It lets the driver watch passenger activity inside the bus.

questions.question: After students unload at a school, the driver should:

options.text: Assume students have taken all their belongings with them.
Assume students have immediately cleared the doorway.
Walk through the bus and check for any sleeping or hiding students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus and check for any sleeping or hiding students.
questions.explanation: After students get off at a school, the driver should walk through the bus to look for any students who are sleeping or hiding. The driver should also check for items students may have left behind.

questions.question: A school bus must be evacuated if:

options.text: The bus has stalled in winter weather.
The air conditioning system has broken.
There is immediate danger of a collision.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is immediate danger of a collision.
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students should stay on the bus. Evacuate the bus if the bus is on railroad tracks, if there is a fire or threat of fire, or if there is a hazardous materials spill. Also evacuate if there is immediate danger of a collision.

questions.question: When checking springs during a vehicle inspection, do all of the following except:

options.text: Make sure torsion springs are not damaged.

questions.explanation: When checking springs during the vehicle inspection test, look for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs and broken or distorted coil springs. If the vehicle has torsion bars, torque arms, or other suspension parts, make sure they are not damaged and are mounted securely.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing while driving a placarded vehicle, you should always:

options.text: Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing in a transit bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle, special rules apply. Stop your vehicle between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Do not stop, change gears, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is crossing the tracks.

questions.question: When unloading students at a school, the driver should:

options.text: Secure the bus by turning off the ignition switch.
Leave the key in the ignition and leave the driver's compartment.
Read a book while students unload.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the bus by turning off the ignition switch.
questions.explanation: When dropping off children at a school, the driver should secure the bus by turning off the ignition. Remove the key if you leave the driver's compartment.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle be parked at the end of the test?

options.text: Exactly where the examiner told you to park it.
Within five feet of where the examiner told you.
Within two feet of where the examiner told you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exactly where the examiner told you to park it.
questions.explanation: Park your vehicle in the exact spot the examiner instructed. If you do not complete the exercise exactly as described, you can fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: What happens if you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic control skills test?

options.text: You get to try the exercise again.
You automatically fail the entire basic control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire basic control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, always face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If driving a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly will cause you to automatically fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: How far behind a school bus should properly adjusted mirrors allow the driver to see?
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors correctly so you can see 200 feet behind the bus. This is equal to about four bus lengths and is important for safe driving.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT required during your on-road driving test?

options.text: Complete the test without an accident.
Use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During your on-road driving test, you must drive safely and responsibly. Wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and laws, and avoid accidents. You should never use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: What should you check about the landing gear during a vehicle inspection?

options.text: That it is more worn on one side than the other.

questions.explanation: During a trailer inspection, make sure the landing gear is fully raised. Check that no parts are missing, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame is not damaged.

questions.question: Is backing a school bus recommended?
questions.explanation: Backing a school bus should be avoided whenever possible. Only back up if there is no other way to move the vehicle.

questions.question: What should students do when approaching a bus stop?

options.text: Stand up and get their belongings.
Walk to the front of the bus and get ready to leave.

questions.explanation: Students must stay seated until told to move. Walking around while the bus is moving is unsafe.

questions.question: Where are outside convex mirrors located on a school bus?
questions.explanation: Outside convex mirrors are placed below the outside flat mirrors. They help you see a wide area around the bus, including traffic and students.

questions.question: How should passengers exit a school bus in an emergency?
questions.explanation: In an emergency, the driver must quickly decide which exit is safest for students and direct them to use it.

questions.question: How many times can you exit your vehicle during the straight line backing exercise?
questions.explanation: You are allowed to exit your vehicle only one time during the straight line backing exercise to check your vehicle's position.
